question: Does the plugin-loading owner accept this registry decomposition after exact-head parity review, direct Codex contract inspection, and a real plugin lifecycle smoke?
rationale: The patch moves central compatibility and security enforcement across many modules without intending behavior changes; automated tests reduce risk but cannot establish that every registration and lifecycle invariant survived the move.

options.title: Require parity proof
options.body: Resolve the boundary check, inspect the touched Codex contracts, and add a redacted live plugin lifecycle transcript before approving the refactor.

options.title: Accept automated coverage
options.body: Merge based on the broad Testbox, build, CI, and static-review evidence while explicitly accepting residual plugin compatibility risk.

options.title: Pause the decomposition
options.body: Leave the monolithic registry in place until the refactor can be split into smaller independently proven domain moves.

recommendation.title: Require parity proof
recommendation.body: Resolve the boundary check, inspect the touched Codex contracts, and add a redacted live plugin lifecycle transcript before approving the refactor.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on manifest-owned plugin loading and activation makes this the strongest independent routing candidate for lifecycle and laziness review.
